name: Ali Alzahrani
headline: Technology leader connecting enterprise IT, industrial operations and practical AI
philosophy: I take ownership of complex challenges, connect ideas across disciplines, and keep working until I find a practical solution.
own_words: I have never faced an issue without providing a solution.
value: For twelve years I have made technology work where it has to: on factory floors, at remote construction sites and across international teams. Today I lead IT for Vallourec's four international sites in the Middle East, and I put AI into people's hands so it does real work.
description: Ali Alzahrani is a Middle East IT Leader based in Saudi Arabia, with twelve years across enterprise IT, industrial technology, cybersecurity coordination and practical AI adoption.

proof.label: years in IT, seven of them in leadership
international sites led across the Middle East
Aramco Cyber Security Certification, led ahead of schedule
remote sites stood up for more than 500 users

traits.name: Resourceful
traits.text: I investigate, learn what I don't yet know and connect ideas from other fields. When a production machine dropped off its application, I went past the edge of my own scope, into the automation hardware, and researched my way to the answer.

traits.name: Accountable
traits.text: I own the outcome, including the part after go-live. During COVID, one technician and I moved seven departments and about 100 people to remote work, and the business kept running.

traits.name: Practical with AI
traits.text: I teach AI where people work, then turn their best ideas into working applications. At home I direct AI agents to build real software, and I test every release myself.

traits.name: Persistent
traits.text: A failed first attempt is information. I narrow a problem by elimination, document what I learned and share it, so the same issue costs less next time.

traits.name: Imaginative
traits.text: I look for the idea nobody asked for. Big touchscreens on the shop floor were my proposal, and they helped move escalation off paper. I also put QR codes at production stations, leading operators to short video lessons.

traits.name: Technical and business-aware
traits.text: I can configure a switch in the morning and defend its budget in the afternoon. I own procurement, contracts and licensing as well as the technology they pay for.

traits.name: A leader who works across people
traits.text: I lead a regional team, work with global functions across time zones and explain complex problems simply, so that non-technical leaders can make clear decisions.

journey: I began my path on a Saudi Aramco scholarship: a preparatory programme in Saudi Arabia, then computer science at the University of Nottingham in the UK and at King Fahd University of Petroleum & Minerals. Along the way I joined leadership programmes in Leeds and Newcastle. I went on to complete a BSc in Information Technology and Computing at the Arab Open University.

My working life started in the hardest possible classroom for an IT person: a construction contractor working for Aramco. As a Project Engineer I directed IT and construction contractors to stand up nine remote sites. Within a year I was Head of IT, responsible for 699 users, a migration to Exchange Online and regaining control of more than 1,000 devices.

In 2017 I joined Vallourec, an industrial manufacturer, as an IT Specialist on the shop floor. That is where I learned how production really runs. I built a QR-code processing application, kept product tracking systems accurate, and was part of the crisis cell during COVID-19. I then spent three years as Infrastructure Expert and Project Manager, mapping the plant's network, leading the Aramco Cyber Security Certification and moving identity and devices to the Microsoft cloud.

Since January 2024 I have been Middle East IT Leader, working across four international sites as the link between the business and our global Business Applications, Infrastructure, Endpoint and Security functions. I also lead regional AI adoption, and that has become central to how I think about the next stage of my career.

contribution.title: A bridge between the business and IT
contribution.text: I listen to what site leaders need, turn it into one clear plan, and work with global teams to deliver it.

contribution.title: Delivery from first requirement to handover
contribution.text: Requirements, design, build, testing, cutover and handover to support, with training and follow-up afterwards.

contribution.title: AI adoption that people actually use
contribution.text: Practical enablement, use-case discovery and working applications, with governance in view from the start.

contribution.title: Stability in demanding environments
contribution.text: I choose the stable, long-term solution over the fastest one. Factories, Aramco requirements and ISO standards taught me why.

contribution.title: Commercial discipline
contribution.text: Vendor selection, negotiation and consolidation, in partnership with Procurement and Finance.

contribution.title: Order where there was none
contribution.text: Procedures, standards, documentation and registers that outlast the project and the person who wrote them.

how_i_work: People know they can count on me. When something important has to get done, managers come to me.
I lead with logic and common sense, and I always think about people too.
I break big projects into small, clear steps. Some days I work with teams in different time zones, and some days I work alone on plans, tests and procedures.
I don't stop at delivery. I train people on the solutions I deliver, and I follow up with them.
